sections.title: Prerequisite: The Area Interpretation of Determinants
sections.content: Briefly explain that the determinant of a 2x2 matrix represents the signed area of the parallelogram formed by the column vectors. Introduce the visual concept of scaling space.
sections.example: Visualizing a square defined by vectors (1,0) and (0,1) transforming into a skewed parallelogram with area |det(A)|.

sections.title: Framing the Linear System
sections.content: Represent the system Ax = b as a vector equation: x1*v1 + x2*v2 = b. Explain that solving for x1 and x2 means finding how much of vector v1 and vector v2 we need to reach the 'target' b.
sections.example: A robot arm with two segments (v1, v2) trying to reach a target point 'b' in a 2D plane.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution (The Cramer's Rule Logic)
sections.content: Show that replacing one column of the matrix with the vector 'b' creates a new parallelogram. Explain that the ratio of the area of this new parallelogram to the original is exactly the scalar value of x1.
sections.example: Swapping v1 with the target vector 'b' creates a new shape. If the area of this new shape is double the original, then x1 must be 2.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize that Cramer's Rule is simply comparing 'areas'. Highlight that x1 = det(A1)/det(A) and x2 = det(A2)/det(A) provides a global view of scaling transformation.
sections.example: A 'Scaling Gauge' animation showing the original unit parallelogram vs. the Cramer-substituted parallelograms as the system solves for 'b'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Area Interpretation of Determinants
lecture_lines: The determinant measures the signed area of a parallelogram.
Unit squares transform into areas scaled by the determinant.
This scaling factor is our fundamental geometric tool.
animations: 1. Create two 2D basis vectors, v_i (#FF6347) and v_j (#4682B4).
2. Define a parallelogram using vectors v_i and v_j.
3. Highlight the area of the parallelogram in #FFFACD.
4. Display the determinant 'det' label (#FFFFFF) near the parallelogram.
5. Transform the parallelogram to show scaling by the determinant.

storyboard.title: Framing the Linear System
lecture_lines: Equations represent building a vector 'b' from v1, v2.
Think of this like a robot arm reaching a target.
Variables x1, x2 define our reach in each direction.
animations: 1. Present a 2D linear system matrix A (#FFD700) and vector x (#00FF00).
2. Show the transformation resulting in vector b (#FF4500).
3. Highlight vectors x and b with labels in #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Geometric Substitution (The Cramer's Rule Logic)
lecture_lines: Replace v1 with 'b' to form a new shape.
The area ratio tells us the scaling factor x1.
This geometric substitution is the core of Cramer's Rule.
animations: 1. Create a 3D volume formed by columns of matrix A.
2. Replace column 1 with vector b (#FF4500) to create a new volume.
3. Compare the original volume and new volume side-by-side.
4. Use a mechanical slider metaphor to adjust the replacement.
5. Show the ratio of volumes as the Cramer's Rule result.

storyboard.title: Visual Synthesis and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Compare the areas of the substituted versus original shapes.
x1 is the ratio of these specific parallelogram areas.
Cramer's Rule interprets linear systems as area scaling.
animations: 1. Summarize all geometric transformations on a single screen.
2. Highlight the relationship between area/volume and determinant.
3. Fade out all elements to black #000000.
